findings.title: The coordinator's master secrets go to every container that reads secrets.env; live, the internet-facing rs-console holds the vault key, worker-token secret and coordinator DB URL
findings.location: trackers/facebook/deploy/docker-compose.console.yml:29-30; deploy/docker-compose.fleetd.yml:52,61; deploy/docker-compose.messenger.yml:37; deploy/docker-compose.poster.yml:36; configs/secrets.env.example:111-121; live container rs-console on 10.10.10.73
findings.evidence: secrets.env carries RS_VAULT_KEY, RS_WORKER_TOKEN_SECRET, RS_ADMIN_TOKEN, RS_CONSOLE_TOKEN and the DB URL. The console, messenger, poster and rs-router compose files all env_file it, and rs_fleetd passes it to every worker as --env-file (fleetd.yml:52). Checked by variable name only: `docker inspect rs-console` shows RS_VAULT_KEY, RS_WORKER_TOKEN_SECRET and RS_DATABASE_URL set. `grep` finds none of the three anywhere in rs_console/rs_console/. fleetd.yml:24 keeps the host token out of secrets.env 'because every worker gets that file', yet host tokens are HMACs of RS_WORKER_TOKEN_SECRET, which is in it. The live fleet-mode workers (TS fleet-agent) do not carry these names.
findings.failure_scenario: rs-console parses ERP traffic and relays VNC websockets behind the Cloudflare tunnel. An RCE or SSRF-to-env in it, or `docker inspect` access on the VM, yields the key that decrypts every account's password and TOTP, the secret that mints any worker or host token, and direct DB access. That is the whole vault, from the one service designed to be 'read-mostly'.
findings.proposed_fix: Split secrets.env: secrets.coordinator.env (vault key, token secret, admin token, DB URL) for the coordinator only; a console file holding RS_CONSOLE_TOKEN plus the admin token it forwards with; a workers' file. Then rotate RS_VAULT_KEY (re-encrypt) and RS_WORKER_TOKEN_SECRET. Recreating the console is not a login; worker recreation is, so plan that rotation with the owner.
findings.regression_test: A test in rs_console or scripts/tests that parses every deploy/*.yml and fails if a service other than the coordinator env_files a file listed as coordinator-only.

findings.title: deploy.sh, AGENTS.md and README describe a VM topology that no longer exists; a deploy now 'verifies' zero workers and posts 'verified' to Telegram
findings.location: trackers/facebook/scripts/deploy.sh:71-73,78-85,182-210,383-416,431-435; trackers/facebook/AGENTS.md 'Versioning, releases, deploys'; VM 10.10.10.73 docker ps
findings.evidence: The VM (docker ps, read-only) has no rs-fleetd container and no compose workers. Nine rs-fleet-homelab-* workers run ghcr.io/jinhuw/aimm-recycle:0.15.0 under the TS rs-fleet-agent (apps/fleet-agent, --restart no). All deploy/docker-compose.homelab*.yml files were deleted (#935-#951). deploy.sh's fleet_mode() checks `docker inspect rs-fleetd`, gets false, and falls to compose mode. homelab_workers() then globs nothing, and verify() loops over zero workers and prints 'verified: every worker and the coordinator run this tree'. The VM stamp .rs-deployed says 0.13.18 (2026-10-24). The VM tree's VERSION is 0.13.18, rs_coordinator/pyproject says 0.14.4 and rs_console says 0.14.16, yet `rsync -nci` shows the code identical to 0.15.0 except those version lines. Deploys have been done by hand since.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator who follows AGENTS.md runs deploy.sh. It force-recreates the coordinator and the console, builds an aimm-recycle:latest image nothing uses, and reports to the Releases topic that the version is on '0 workers - verified running this tree'. The fleet stays on whatever GHCR tag the ERP released. Meanwhile /healthz versions (0.14.x) disagree with the code, so version-based drift checks give wrong answers. AGENTS.md also still says to use `rsc fleet release`, which now drives an agent that is not running.
findings.proposed_fix: Retire or rewrite deploy.sh for the current split: coordinator and console only, workers via push-fleet-images.sh plus the ERP's POST /api/fleet/releases. Make verify fail when it found zero workers. Update AGENTS.md/README/deploy/README.md. Stamp the VM's VERSION and pyprojects consistently (needs owner).
findings.regression_test: test: run deploy.sh's verify with an empty homelab_workers list and assert a non-zero exit.

findings.title: deploy.sh never checks the vendored monitor against VENDOR.md; it ships and builds whatever clone is on disk
findings.evidence: release.sh:104 runs check-vendor.sh, and so does push-fleet-images.sh:69-72. deploy.sh does not (grep finds no call). check-release-tag.sh's `git status --porcelain -- .` ignores the gitignored ai-marketplace-monitor/. deploy.sh then rsyncs ai-marketplace-monitor and builds the worker image from it. verify_worker compares the container against the same local clone, so a drifted clone reads MATCH.
findings.failure_scenario: A deploy from a worktree whose clone sits on a different commit, or carries uncommitted edits, ships an unpinned monitor under a valid release tag. Today's worktrees show four different clone HEADs (gar-2 ac161ad, milkfish f4d4fdf, telescopefish 93e2566, pin 3576db7). The Releases log then names a version whose engine nobody can reconstruct, which is the 'lost pin' incident of 2026-10-23 again.
findings.proposed_fix: Call `sh scripts/check-vendor.sh` in deploy.sh's version gate, before the rsync.
findings.regression_test: scripts/tests: fixture repo with a vendored clone off-pin; assert deploy.sh's gate step refuses.

findings.title: A seeded pool cookie (cookie-first Assign) is overwritten by the slot's previous login's backup, and the restore the ERP queued then 409s; the worker falls back to a password login
findings.evidence: backup_session accepts any jar with an xs cookie. When its uid is not the slot account's, _session_identity returns None. upsert_snapshot then replaces the row unconditionally, including the snapshot seed_session just sealed. session.py:100-103 itself says the previous login's session is 'still being saved while a swap's re-login is on its way'. Reproduced in docs/review-2026-10-31/repro/A10/test_seed_overwritten_by_stale_backup.py, which passes: after seed + stale backup, fb_user_id is the old uid and restore returns 409. Also, with the legacy fleet token, backup_session takes worker_id from the body (session.py:158), so any legacy-token holder can replace any worker's snapshot.
findings.failure_scenario: The ERP assigns a pool account by cookie: PUT /session, then POST /restore-session. The worker's periodic backup of the old login lands first, and the seeded cookie is lost. The restore is refused, so the worker logs in by password + 2FA. That is the checkpoint-prone path the cookie-first assign exists to avoid.
findings.proposed_fix: In backup_session, when the slot's account has a uid and the incoming session's uid differs, refuse with 409 (or store it in a side column), never replacing a restorable snapshot. Require require_own_worker semantics (no legacy token) for backups.
findings.regression_test: The repro test above, inverted: assert the stale backup is refused and restore still returns 200.

findings.title: Telegram MarkdownV2 escaping omits the backslash and truncates after escaping; such an alert fails with 400 and is retried forever
findings.evidence: _MARKDOWN_V2_SPECIALS = r"_*[]()~`>#+-=|{}.!" has no '\'. send() posts text[:4096] of already-escaped text with parse_mode MarkdownV2.
findings.failure_scenario: A seller title ending in '\' (e.g. 'R730 64GB\') escapes the template's closing '*'. Telegram answers 400 'can't find end of Bold entity'. The outbox retries every 15 min forever, the listing is stored as seen, and the buy lead is never alerted. A 4096-char cut through an escape pair does the same.
findings.proposed_fix: Escape '\' first. Truncate raw fields before escaping. On a 400 parse error, resend without parse_mode or mark the row dead with an ops note.
findings.regression_test: test_telegram_notify: escape_markdown('a\\') round-trip; a 5000-char title produces valid MarkdownV2.

findings.title: Nothing enforces one account per worker; the CLI skips the API's 409
findings.evidence: accounts.worker_id has no unique index. account_row_for_worker is `SELECT * ... WHERE worker_id = ?` + fetchone() with no ORDER BY. The API's check-then-write 409 is racy, and `rsc vault set-account --worker` performs no check.
findings.failure_scenario: Two rows map to va-1. On Postgres, which row comes back can change after any UPDATE. The worker is then handed the other account's password or TOTP, identity and restore checks run against the wrong uid, and a login under the wrong device follows.
findings.proposed_fix: Partial unique index on accounts(worker_id) WHERE worker_id IS NOT NULL in both backends, after a dedupe. The CLI refuses like the API.
findings.regression_test: test_accounts: second set-account for the same worker via CLI raises; DB-level unique violation test.

findings.title: Any worker token can ack another worker's queued Messenger reply, and fetch has no claim/lease, so replies can be dropped or sent twice
findings.evidence: ack_outbound ignores the authenticated worker and only checks that the id exists (lines 163-176). fetch_outbound is a plain SELECT of status='queued'. With the legacy token and no worker_id it returns every worker's queue. Matrix replies have worker_id NULL.
findings.failure_scenario: Two rs-router pollers, or a slow ack overlapping the next poll, both send the same staff reply to a seller. Or a buggy or compromised worker acks someone else's reply as sent and it is silently lost.
findings.proposed_fix: ack requires worker == row.worker_id. Fetch claims atomically (UPDATE ... SET status='sending', claimed_at ... RETURNING) with a lease that expires back to queued.
findings.regression_test: test_messages: worker B acking A's row gets 403; two concurrent fetches return disjoint rows.

findings.title: Concurrent incident reports lose votes and can page DOWN twice
findings.evidence: get_incident, then incidents.apply in Python, then a blind save_incident upsert, with no lock on either backend.
findings.failure_scenario: An AI-provider outage makes the whole fleet report 'down' within seconds. Two handlers both see 'closed' and both page DOWN. The last writer's reporters JSON wins, so a later single 'up' closes the incident and pages 'recovered' while workers whose votes were lost are still down, and they never re-vote.
findings.proposed_fix: Serialize with a process lock (as city_queue._handout does) or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on Postgres.
findings.regression_test: Threaded test posting N concurrent 'down' reports; assert one page and N reporters.

findings.title: A worker with no account mapping can lock any account it names
findings.evidence: _account_for falls back to payload.account_id when resolve_account fails. A challenge with kind=='locked' then runs db.lock_account(account_id).
findings.failure_scenario: A freshly provisioned or detached worker (or a compromised one) posts {kind:'locked', account_id:<any>}. From then on no worker is handed that account's password until `rsc vault unlock`, and the healthy account silently drops out of the fleet.
findings.proposed_fix: Lock only the account resolved from the worker's own mapping; keep the claimed id only as challenge metadata.
findings.regression_test: test_escalation: unmapped worker posting locked for account X leaves X unlocked.

findings.title: A listing whose alert enqueue fails is stored as seen and never alerted
findings.evidence: claim_listing/update_listing commit in one call. enqueue_alert runs later in a separate call. An exception between them only counts the listing as 'failed'.
findings.failure_scenario: A DB blip or pool timeout between claim and enqueue leaves the listing committed. Every later sighting is a DUPLICATE, so the lead is lost. For a DISCOUNTED listing the new price is already stored, so the drop can't be detected again.
findings.proposed_fix: Claim/update and enqueue in one transaction, or a reconciler that alerts listings with no outbox row.
findings.regression_test: test_outbox: make enqueue_alert raise once; assert a retry or the next sighting still alerts.

findings.title: Settings save writes some worker configs, fails on a fleet write, and leaves settings.json on the old values
findings.evidence: apply() renders everything first, then writes the mounted files and then fleet configs one by one (fleet.write). A FleetError (OSError) on worker N becomes a 500 in put_settings before settings.save(state) runs.
findings.failure_scenario: During a coordinator blip the ERP reports 'save failed', yet some workers already search with the new keywords or cities while the saved state and /v1/fleet show the old ones. The next render (deploy, or the next save) silently reverts those workers.
findings.proposed_fix: Save the state before the fleet writes, or continue past failed fleet writes and return the failures with the state saved.
findings.regression_test: test_settings: fleet.write raises on the 2nd worker; assert settings.json carries the new values and the response lists the failure.

findings.title: A blocking coordinator call inside the async VNC/fleet handlers, behind a threading.Lock, stalls the whole console; an unauthenticated websocket can trigger it
findings.evidence: _fleet_vnc_targets() calls fleet.state() (a sync httpx call, 10 s timeout) under threading.Lock every 30 s when its cache expires. It is called from async def vnc_socket before the ticket is checked (line 539), and from the /v1/fleet builder.
findings.failure_scenario: With a slow coordinator, every cache refresh freezes the event loop for up to 10 s. Live VNC bridges stall and the ERP's proxied reads time out. Anyone who can reach the console's websocket can trigger a refresh without a token.
findings.proposed_fix: Use await asyncio.to_thread(_vnc_targets), or an async client with asyncio.Lock, and check the ticket is present before resolving targets.
findings.regression_test: Async test with a fake fleet that sleeps 2 s: a concurrent /healthz must answer in well under 2 s.

findings.title: A worker-supplied vnc_url is rendered as a clickable href with no scheme check
findings.evidence: The heartbeat stores payload.vnc_url, a free str, as given. /v1/fleet passes it through, and fleet.js uses w.vnc_url ?? ... as an href after esc(), which escapes HTML but not URL schemes. On challenge rows ch.vnc_url wins over the console's own viewer.
findings.failure_scenario: A compromised worker heartbeats vnc_url 'javascript:...'. An operator clicks Watch on the console page, where the console token sits in localStorage. Whether it executes depends on browser handling of target=_blank/noopener, so this is a path, not a demonstrated exploit. The ERP's React page consumes the same field.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept only http(s) or same-origin /vnc/ URLs, both at heartbeat time on the coordinator and in watchButton. Prefer vncFor() over ch.vnc_url.
findings.regression_test: test_coordinator: heartbeat with javascript: vnc_url is rejected (422).

findings.title: The documented ERP contract omits the two session routes the ERP uses, and rs_console's safety docstring overstates its blast radius
findings.evidence: PUT /v1/workers/{id}/session (seal a live cookie) and POST /v1/workers/{id}/restore-session are forwarded (app.py:360, 281) and called by apps/backend/src/routes/facebookPool.ts:680,689, but neither is in AGENTS.md's forwarded list. The docstring says 'no auth/credential/session route is forwarded' and that a token compromise 'yields fleet metadata, not accounts'. Yet the token can write fb_uid via PUT /v1/accounts/{id}, seed a matching cookie and queue relogins. Paragraph 23-28 is duplicated at 30-35.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone pruning routes 'not in the contract' breaks Assign. Or someone sizes the console token's risk from the docstring and under-protects it.
findings.proposed_fix: List both session routes (and that they carry a login) in AGENTS.md and the root contract table; rewrite the threat-model paragraph.
findings.regression_test: test_console already pins the route set; add the two session routes to an explicit documented allowlist assertion.

findings.title: The poster/messenger account lock checks liveness by PID across separate containers' PID namespaces
findings.evidence: The lock stores os.getpid() and tests liveness with os.kill(pid, 0). Poster and messenger run in different containers, each with tini as PID 1, so PIDs are small, collide, and are meaningless across namespaces. Stale-break is unlink-then-create, which races, and finally unlinks even a lock this process no longer owns.
findings.failure_scenario: A messenger killed while holding the lock restarts with the same PID, sees 'itself' alive and exits with SessionLockedError, and the bridge stays down until someone deletes account.lock. Or the other container sees 'no such process' and breaks a live lock, so poster and messenger drive one Facebook account at once, which is the very thing the lock exists to prevent.
findings.proposed_fix: fcntl.flock on the lock file in the shared volume: the kernel releases it when the holder dies, across containers on one host.
findings.regression_test: Test: two processes with different PID namespaces simulated via a stub os.kill; assert a held flock blocks and a dead holder frees it.

findings.title: A legacy Mac monitor and a daily headless session probe still run from the archived checkout, outside the fleet and its device and proxy rules
findings.location: launchd jobs com.recycleservers.fbmonitor (live pid running ~/Projects/recycle_servers/facebook_tracker/.venv-aimm/bin/aimm) and com.recycleservers.search-probe; trackers/facebook/scripts/probe-search-url.py:163-166; deploy/com.recycleservers.search-probe.plist
findings.evidence: `launchctl list` shows com.recycleservers.fbmonitor running (last exit -15) plus search-probe and keyword-eval. Per the sub-review, the probe ran today at 07:46 from the legacy checkout (last commit 2026-10-16). probe-search-url.py opens storage_state=args.session headless with no proxy, device identity or account lock. The repo's plists point at /Users/jinhu/Development/..., which does not exist.
findings.failure_scenario: A Facebook account is logged in daily from the office IP with a headless fingerprint, and a full monitor keeps searching from stale code. Neither shows up in the fleet ledger, so a checkpoint on that account looks unexplained.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner decision: unload the legacy fbmonitor and the probe, or move them to the repo checkout with headed browser, proxy and identity from the sidecar, or use the logged-out resolver. Fix the plist paths. Do not stop them without the owner.
findings.regression_test: n/a (operational).

findings.title: browse-session.py saves the session every 5 s without a logged-in guard, proxy fallback, device identity or lock
findings.evidence: ctx.storage_state(path=sess) runs every 5 s with no xs/is_logged_in check, which is the bug session.py:231-241 guards against. The write is not atomic and has no indexed_db. The proxy comes only from --proxy, and there is no identity.json or account_lock.
findings.failure_scenario: A checkpoint or logout while warming a session, or a forgotten --proxy, overwrites a good saved session with a logged-out jar or replays it from the operator's IP. Rebuilding costs a password + 2FA login.
findings.proposed_fix: Reuse PosterSession (device_context_options and proxy_settings from the sidecar). Save via atomic_write_text only when xs is present. Take the account lock.
findings.regression_test: Unit test with a fake context whose cookies lack xs: assert the file is unchanged.

findings.title: `rs-session check` opens a live session under a different device, and the README schedules `check --save-refreshed`
findings.evidence: The check context sets only the user agent and a fixed 1440x900 viewport: no device_context_options (screen, scale, locale, timezone) and no account_lock. --save-refreshed rewrites the session file while the worker's browser holds it.
findings.failure_scenario: A routine cron check presents a second device fingerprint on the account and can revert the worker's rotated cookies, leading to session invalidation and a re-login.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply device_context_options and account_lock as session.py:195-197 does. Document `info` as the cron-safe command and `check` as an operator action.
findings.regression_test: test_session_cli: check builds context kwargs identical to PosterSession's for the same sidecar.

findings.title: Re-capturing a session without --proxy keeps the old proxy in its sidecar
findings.evidence: `if value: meta[key] = value` never clears a key, so a capture without a proxy leaves the previous proxy in place.
findings.failure_scenario: A session first captured through proxy X is re-captured on the house IP. PosterSession (session.py:200) and check then replay it through X, the IP-mismatch pattern master.toml says causes revocations.
findings.proposed_fix: On capture and import, write proxy explicitly, deleting it when absent.
findings.regression_test: test_cookies: capture with proxy, then without; assert meta has no proxy.

findings.title: rs-router reuses Matrix transaction ids after each restart, and treats transient errors as permanent; staff replies are silently dropped
findings.evidence: self._txn starts at 0 in every process, so transaction ids repeat as rsrouter-1, rsrouter-2, .... Matrix dedupes PUT /send/{txnId} per access token and returns the earlier event without sending. drain_outbound acks every MatrixError, timeouts and 5xx included, with permanent=True.
findings.failure_scenario: After any router restart, the first N staff replies return 200 with an old event id and are acked 'sent', so the seller never gets them. During a homeserver restart, replies are marked permanently failed.
findings.proposed_fix: txnId = f'rsrouter-{row["id"]}' (idempotent per outbound row). Treat URLError and 5xx as retryable.
findings.regression_test: test_bridge: two MatrixClient instances send different rows; assert distinct txn ids; a 503 is acked non-permanent.

findings.title: check-secrets.sh misses the files .gitignore protects as credentials and unquoted or lowercase secret values
findings.evidence: The path list lacks configs/secrets.*.env (e.g. secrets.fleetd.env), configs/account_info.txt* (passwords + 2FA), proxies.decodo.txt, data.txt and *.local.toml. The content rule needs an upper-case key with a quoted value, so RS_VAULT_KEY=abc..., "totp_secret": "...", user:pass@ proxy URLs, postgres URLs and syt_ tokens all pass. Any line containing '...' is whitelisted.
findings.failure_scenario: A force-added secrets.fleetd.env or account_info.txt passes the release gate (release.sh runs it) and lands in history.
findings.proposed_fix: Mirror the .gitignore credential block. Add an unquoted KEY=value rule, case-insensitive matching, and URL-credential and syt_ patterns.
findings.regression_test: Extend scripts/tests/test-check-secrets.sh with each missed case.

findings.title: Re-login (a Facebook login) records no actor and has no server-side cooldown
findings.evidence: Only relogin_last_requested_at is stored, with no updated_by; the only confirmation is window.confirm in vnc.js:150. A press after each directive poll is another login. Mitigated by the 2/day password budget (auth.py:88-95).
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: Forward and store requested_by; 409 within N minutes of the last request.

findings.title: Console path params for relogin, queue and cities are not validated; a bad id upserts a phantom worker row
findings.evidence: These lack the _WORKER_ID check the session/logins routes have. The allowlist can't be escaped, but request_relogin upserts any id, which then shows in /v1/fleet.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply _WORKER_ID on all three.

findings.title: Legacy fleet token can consume other workers' directives and leases; a per-worker token's mismatched path id is ignored, not refused
findings.evidence: `worker or worker_id` skips the ownership check when worker is None.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: require_own_worker semantics; retire RS_COORDINATOR_TOKEN.

findings.title: Settings CLI (start-at) and the API can overwrite each other's saves
findings.evidence: _settings_lock is per-process; the CLI does load, modify and save outside it.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: fcntl.flock around load/apply/save.

findings.title: vnc TicketStore is touched from threadpool and event loop without a lock
findings.evidence: _prune iterates the dict while issue() inserts from another thread; rare 'dictionary changed size' 500.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: Lock, or make vnc_ticket async.

findings.title: Non-ASCII bearer token gives 500 instead of 401
findings.evidence: secrets.compare_digest(str,str) raises TypeError on non-ASCII input.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: Compare .encode() bytes.

findings.title: Public /vnc/{worker_id} reveals which worker ids exist
findings.evidence: Answers 404 or 200 without a token, and triggers the A10-12 coordinator fetch.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: Always serve the shell.

findings.evidence: apply_queue/apply_tiers run only when rows is not None, which contradicts AGENTS.md ('Both are null').
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: apply_queue(doc, None) in the else branch.

findings.title: Ops pages from request handlers are sent inline and dropped during a Telegram outage
findings.evidence: Direct ops_notifier.send (30 s timeout, shared pacing lock) rather than the outbox.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: db.enqueue_alert as the incidents path does.

findings.evidence: ensure_topic trusts the stored id; sends retry with it forever.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: On 'thread not found', clear and recreate.

findings.title: Any worker token reads every worker's raw row

findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.

findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.

findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.

findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.

findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.

findings.title: make-region-config.py swaps the proxy server but keeps the homelab proxy's credentials

findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.

findings.title: Coordinator LAN override and the live haproxy relay both bind 10.10.10.73:8500; the LAN/registry docs rely on ufw, which Docker-published ports bypass
findings.evidence: Live: rs-coordinator-lan is the haproxy relay on 10.10.10.73:8500. configs/secrets.coordinator-lan.env is absent, so deploy.sh takes the plain path today. Creating that file (per the registry docs) makes the next coordinator recreate fail on 'port already allocated'.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.

findings.title: Floating image tags on services holding a Facebook session; messenger built FROM aimm-recycle:latest

findings.title: Terraform for the coordinator Postgres keeps local state and protects only the service
findings.evidence: State (the only copy of the generated password and mapping) is local and lost with a worktree. prevent_destroy is on railway_service.postgres but not railway_project. The DB has no snapshots and a public TCP proxy.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: Remote backend; prevent_destroy on the project; scheduled pg_dump to R2.

findings.title: rs-poster post can duplicate an ad@city; the ledger upsert orphans the first listing
findings.evidence: Only max_active_ads is checked.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: Refuse if an active ledger row exists for ad@city.

findings.title: build-monitor-image.sh stamps the ERP repo's commit as RS_MONITOR_COMMIT, and its dirty check can never fire
findings.evidence: `git -C $ROOT rev-parse` is the monorepo HEAD, and ai-marketplace-monitor is gitignored there, so status is always clean. deploy.sh:339 and push-fleet-images.sh:79 use the clone's own HEAD.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: git -C $ROOT/ai-marketplace-monitor rev-parse / status.

findings.title: release.sh doesn't run rs_router's tests or bump its version; rs_fleetd is now dormant on the VM
findings.evidence: rs_router is deployed (matrix compose) but is outside the gate and the version sweep. The VM runs no rs-fleetd (the TS fleet-agent replaced it), yet deploy.sh, AGENTS.md and `rsc fleet release` still treat it as the rollout path.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
findings.proposed_fix: Add rs_router to run_suite and the bump list; mark rs_fleetd legacy or remove it.

findings.title: VM keeps seven secrets.env.bak-* copies, including ones from before the 2026-10-22 rotation
findings.evidence: secrets.env.bak-20261004 through -20261023-rs375 (pre- and post-rotation). The rsync filter protects /configs/secrets.env.*, so they persist indefinitely.
findings.failure_scenario: See evidence: narrow impact as described.
